eraSoftware: MACRO-11, FORTRAN IV, BASIC-PLUS, DIBOL and the DECUS tape library
museum.periodBrowser: none — a decade before the web, on a glass teletype
museum.blurb: One machine and three of the operating systems DEC sold for it — a real-time monitor, a real-time executive and a timesharing system — because in 1975 you did not buy a computer with an operating system, you bought a computer and then chose one.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile, and the oldest machine in the collection. Emulator-in-captured-Linux BRIDGE tile: a captured Debian 13 (trixie) kiosk runs one fullscreen green-on-black xterm whose only program is a chooser, and pressing 1, 2 or 3 boots RT-11 V5.3, RSX-11M V4.2 BL38 or RSTS/E V9.6 under Open SIMH (pinned at commit a1f57fa3 and built INTO this tile's overlay, the amiga.sh precedent, because the frozen bridge base predates it). ONE tile rather than three because a visitor cannot tell RT-11's “.” from RSX-11M's “>” from RSTS/E's “Ready”, and three near-identical terminals would read as one exhibit cloned by accident; the chooser is the placard. THE VERSIONS ARE THE MENTEC CEILINGS: the 1997 hobbyist grant covers RT-11 V5.3, RSTS/E V9.6, RSX-11M V4.3 and RSX-11M-PLUS V3.0 “or prior”, which is exactly why they are hard to find. RSX-11M is V4.2 and the exhibit says V4.2 — V4.3 media is not reachable anywhere today, and the community's RSX-11M-PLUS V4.6 and RSTS/E V10.1 are outside the grant. RSTS/E is installed as far as its media allows: the pack boots to timesharing and a working DCL $ prompt, but DEC's procedure ends by asking for a second “Library” tape that is not in the kit and is not obtainable, so START.COM and the packaged CCL commands are absent — the chooser says so in three lines of its own text rather than leaving a visitor to discover it. The golden idles AT the chooser with no simulator running, so a tile nobody is watching costs nothing, and each system runs on a fresh sparse copy of its pack. Keyboard-only exhibit; mono-terminal archetype. The arc worth reading aloud: the “>” of RSX-11M is the prompt whose authors, under Dave Cutler, went on to write VMS and then Windows NT, both of which are already in this gallery. See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md and docs/guests/decos.md.

reset.fixture: The PDP-11 chooser: a green-on-black 80x31 xterm on a 1024x768 X root naming RT-11 V5.3, RSX-11M V4.2 and RSTS/E V9.6 with the prompt each answers with, over “Press 1, 2 or 3. Reset returns you to this screen.” The RSTS/E line carries its own three-line caveat about the missing Library tape. The golden holds NO running simulator, so reset both returns the visitor to the placard and throws away the session. Certified 2026-08-09 after the bake, by framebuffer: the 80-column rule measured x=3..962 of 1024 on the cold boot, on the restore, and again after the keyboard proof; pressing 1 through QMP input-send-event left the chooser and started a pdp11 process at RT-11FB V05.03, pressing 3 reached RSTS/E V9.6 timesharing and a DCL $, and loadvm golden brought the bare chooser back with no simulator running. Keyboard-only exhibit (no pointer device); AC97 present but the guest makes no sound.
